marks.gloss_en: the mishna: there is no difference between vow-offerings and gift-offerings except responsibility
hence, regarding [the prohibition] 'do not delay', both are alike
which is a vow? one who says: a burnt-offering is upon me
R' Shimon (in the baraita): the law of responsibility is read from 'and it shall be accepted for him to atone upon him'
R' Yitzchak bar Avdimi: since he said 'upon me', he is like one who carries it on his shoulder
דריסת הרגל? הא לא קפדי אינשי! -- stepping-foot is no benefit people mind; why should it be forbidden?
הא מני — רבי אליעזר, דאמר: ויתור אסור במודר הנאה (= p_mishna_kerabbi_eliezer, p_vitur_asur)
people are not particular about [others stepping on their property]
the mishna: the one forbidden all benefit from his fellow differs from the one forbidden his food in stepping-foot [which is forbidden to the former]
the mishna excepts only vessels with which food is NOT prepared, so for vessels with which food is prepared the two are alike (marker: the bare הא; see header)
it follows that with regard to vessels with which food is prepared, this one and that one are equal
והלא דין הוא: if the two-sighting zav renders couch and seat impure, should he not require the count of seven?
הא -- from 'only the offering' it follows that for couch and seat the two are equal
הא -- from 'only the offering' it follows that for the seven-day count the two are equal
so with regard to (rendering impure) a couch and a seat, this and that are equal
מנהני מילי? דתנו רבנן: רבי סימאי אומר ... שתים לטומאה (kind svara: no support kind for a plain דתנו רבנן citation)
R' Simai: the verse counted two and called him impure, three and called him impure; how so? two for impurity and three for the offering
דתניא: מזובו -- some zavim bring and some do not: three bring, two do not (the mishna's offering difference)
(entertained) two for the offering and not for impurity; three for impurity as well
there is no difference between a zav who sees two sightings and one who sees three except the offering
(entertained) two for impurity and not for the offering; three for the offering and not for impurity
(entertained by the baraita) or perhaps: two sightings bring, three do not
the verse-word: 'and when the zav is cleansed from his flux' (Lev 15:13) -- what is derived from it?
'and when the zav is cleansed': when he ceases from his flux
